130: 
131: ### 9. Verify what can be verified
132: 
133: Run the safe, relevant checks the project offers. Inspect the rendered interface when runtime behavior or visual judgment matters, and report the exact command or interaction and its result. A check you cannot run is **Not verified**, never a finding.
134: 
135: ### 10. Review without mutating by default
136: 
137: Treat a review request as read-only. Do not edit source unless the user also asks you to implement the findings. When they do, keep the consolidated report as the change scope and re-run the relevant verification afterward.
138: 
139: ## Before you finish
140: 
141: | Mistake | Fix |
142: | --- | --- |
143: | Six disconnected domain reports | One ranked findings table |
144: | Visual claim inferred only from source | Inspect the rendered state, or mark it not verified |
145: | Silent gaps in coverage | Show which domains and states were actually inspected |
146: | Missing owning skill treated as covered | Mark the domain `Not reviewed` and name the skill |
147: | Every legacy issue in a touched file reported | Three pre-existing findings, in their own section |
148: | A pre-existing issue blocking a change review | Keep pre-existing findings out of the cap and out of the verdict |
149: | Domain marked `Clear` when the change never touched it | Mark it `Not reviewed: no evidence in the change scope` |
150: 
151: ## Review output format
152: 
153: The format lives in [review-format.md](review-format.md): scope and coverage, the findings table, verification and the verdict. A review is not finished until its findings are reported there.
